package_info.package_manager: standalone tool (not a package manager, but used in attack chain)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (tool usage, not a library vulnerability)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack leverages input fuzzing and Unicode encoding to bypass phone number uniqueness validation in OpenAI's account signup API, enabling mass abuse of free credits by registering multiple accounts with the same phone number.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (API request manipulation during account signup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During account signup, the attacker modifies the phone_number field by prepending zeros to create a variant of the same phone number, bypassing uniqueness checks and enabling multiple account registrations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate users should not need to manipulate phone number formatting to bypass validation. The use of leading zeros is a known technique to evade naive uniqueness checks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects phone numbers to be normalized and validated for uniqueness before account creation. Here, the system fails to normalize before uniqueness check.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some international phone number formats may include leading zeros, but not in this context where the intent is to bypass validation.
key_indicators: Multiple accounts tied to the same underlying phone number

execution_context.trigger: runtime (API request manipulation during account signup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During account signup, the attacker injects Unicode escape sequences (e.g., \u000a) into the phone_number field, creating unique variants that bypass upstream uniqueness checks but are normalized downstream, allowing multiple accounts with the same phone number.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting non-printable Unicode characters into a phone number field is highly abnormal and indicative of an attempt to bypass input validation or exploit normalization inconsistencies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Phone numbers should only contain digits and possibly standard formatting characters. Unicode escapes are not expected or legitimate in this context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for Unicode escapes in phone numbers in standard web forms.
key_indicators: Presence of Unicode escape sequences in phone number fields
Multiple accounts with visually identical phone numbers differing only by encoding

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker uses the recollapse tool to automatically generate and test multiple phone number variants with different encodings and positions of Unicode escapes, automating the bypass of uniqueness checks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated fuzzing of input fields to discover bypasses is a common attacker technique and not part of normal user or developer behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal account creation does not involve automated input mutation or fuzzing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security researchers may use such tools for testing, but not in production or user-facing workflows.
key_indicators: Automated input mutation targeting validation logic
High volume of similar requests with minor input variations

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers an account with a valid phone number.
attack_chain.leads_to: Phone number is associated with an account and receives free credits.

attack_chain.action: Attacker attempts to register additional accounts with the same phone number, but is blocked by uniqueness validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: No free credits granted; uniqueness check triggers.

attack_chain.action: Attacker manipulates the phone_number field by prepending zeros or injecting Unicode escapes to create unique variants.
Attacker automates the process using the recollapse tool to generate many phone number variants.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass registration of accounts, each receiving free credits.

attack_chain.action: Downstream normalization collapses all variants to the same phone number, but only after credits are granted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker controls multiple accounts with the same phone number and accumulates free credits.

behavioral_signatures: Multiple account registrations using phone numbers with leading zeros or Unicode escapes
High volume of account creation attempts from the same IP or device fingerprint
API requests with non-digit characters or escape sequences in phone_number fields
file_indicators: Unusual phone number formats in account database (e.g., leading zeros, Unicode escapes)
Logs showing repeated /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify requests with minor phone_number variations
network_indicators: Burst of POST requests to /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify with similar phone numbers
Patterns of account creation from the same network segment
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor account creation API endpoints for phone_number fields containing leading zeros, non-digit characters, or Unicode escape sequences. Flag multiple account registrations tied to phone numbers that normalize to the same value. Implement normalization and validation at the earliest point in the workflow and log/alert on attempts to bypass with encoding tricks or fuzzed input.
